                                         To address this, we introduce a dual-memory augmented
                                         HMR critique agent with self-reflection to produce context-

                                         distill fine-grained cues about 3D human motion structure,
                                         physical feasibility, and alignment with the input image.

                                         This paper aims to tackle the challenge of monocular human

                                         mesh recovery (HMR), which involves estimating both hu-
                                                                                                          tion quality. However, the image-driven scorer can be mis-

                                         3D human perception is crucial for understanding activities
                                                                                                          poses. In challenging scenarios, such as occlusion or in-
                                         and enabling applications such as VR, robotics, and gam-

                                         ing. However, this task is inherently ill-posed, as lifting 2D
                                                                                                          often provides unreliable guidance. This is because DPO
                                         observations to 3D motion is highly ambiguous.
                                                                                                          relies only on pairwise comparisons and ignores the quality

Figure 2. Overview of our framework. Our purpose is to refine a diffusion-based HMR model that generates a group of human mesh
predictions per input image. We propose a VLM-enhanced HMR critique agent that assigns a score for each human mesh prediction.
This critique agent is equipped with a dual-memory mechanism to give stable assessments. Then, we use this critique agent to build a
group-wise HMR preference dataset without the need for manual labeling. Finally, we employ this preference dataset to finetune the base
model to preferentially generate predictions that are physically plausible and better aligned with the image cues.

reflection to retrieve judging rules and visual prototypes,                                  Human Feedback (RLHF) to a group-wise formulation,
enabling consistent and semantically grounded evaluation                                     providing more stable policy updates while removing the
without finetuning.                                                                          need for a separate value model. For each condition c, a

4.3. HMR Critique Agent Results                                                                 line’s “Initial score” is unreliable and appears to lack 3D
Evaluation protocol. To evaluate the critique agent, we                                         awareness: it assigns a high score to a flawed pose (a) and
use two protocols: point-wise and group-wise. Point-wise                                        an incorrectly low score to a high-quality 3D mesh (d). In
evaluation assesses the agent’s ability to predict the absolute                                 contrast, our critique agent demonstrates a robust compre-
quality of each single prediction, while group-wise evalua-                                     hension of the 3D action and geometry. It correctly identi-
tion tests its ability to rank the relative quality of K pre-                                   fies that poses (a) and (c) fail to capture the proper surfing
dictions for the same image. Our point-wise benchmark                                           stance, especially the incorrectly extended left arm. Our
is identical to that of ADHMR, using single perturbed GT                                        agent also identifies major 3D geometric failures such as
poses to simulate predictions. For group-wise evaluation,                                       severe self-penetration (b, c). This shows our agent’s feed-
we generate K distinct predictions per image and compute                                        back is grounded in a precise understanding of 3D human
correlation within each group, reporting the mean across                                        motion, allowing it to identify subtle errors, thus rectifying
groups. We calibrate the critique agent’s outputs to the                                        the base model’s flawed assessments via our group prefer-
HMR-Scorer’s numeric range using a quadratic program-                                           ence optimization framework.
